paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this one: when God's people take His Word seriously, it shows up in the details. Josiah doesn't just feel good about what was found in the Book of the Law. He tells the Levites to "carry out the word of the LORD given by Moses" (2 Chronicles 35:6), and then everybody gets a job, a place and a plan. Following God was never meant to stay a nice idea in your head, baker.

And look at who's giving. Josiah gives from his own flocks and herds (2 Chronicles 35:7), and his officials contribute willingly (2 Chronicles 35:8). Nobody is dragged into this one. The Levites even make preparations for the priests and for the gatekeepers, so nobody has to leave their post (2 Chronicles 35:14, 15). I know a little about being the one who gets left in the back, friend, and this is what it looks like when God's people look out for each other.

So what does it mean for you? The text says "No such Passover had been observed in Israel since the days of Samuel the prophet" (2 Chronicles 35:18). That's what happens when people hear God's Word, believe it and do it together. Open the Word, do what it says, and bring the ones next to you along. That's my kind of kitchen, and Josiah's story isn't over yet.
